info.name: Codemare compile service
info.description:
Requests for the Codemare compile service (`backend/`): the stateless executor the web app calls to judge code.

- `GET /health` (open)
- `POST /v1/run` and `POST /v1/run/stream` (SSE): run code against caller-supplied tests
- `POST /v1/ide/execute` and `GET /v1/ide/execute/:token`: stdin/stdout programs
- `GET /v1/queue/stats`: the optional IDE-mode queue

Everything under `/v1` needs `X-Codemare-Token` when the service has `INTERNAL_TOKEN` set (always in production). Every request here sends `{{internalToken}}` from the environment; leave it empty for a local dev service without a token.

Default `{{baseUrl}}`: http://localhost:4000. See backend/postman/README.md.

request.description: Liveness probe. Open: no token needed (load balancers and container healthchecks call it).

item.name: 02 - Run (POST /v1/run)
item.description: The pure executor: the caller sends the code and the tests, the service answers with per-test results and a verdict (OK, WA, TLE, MLE, RE, CE, XX). Always runs inline, never through the queue.

exec: pm.test("Every test result carries idx, hidden, passed, runUs, wallUs, memoryKb, actual", function () {

request.description: Judge a Python solution against the tests in the body. `signature` is optional for Python, JavaScript and TypeScript.
Judge a JavaScript solution against the tests in the body. `signature` is optional for Python, JavaScript and TypeScript.
Judge a TypeScript solution against the tests in the body. `signature` is optional for Python, JavaScript and TypeScript. TypeScript is transpiled in the service, then runs as JavaScript.
Judge a C++ solution against the tests in the body. C++, Java and Go need `signature`: their harnesses are generated from typed literals.
Judge a Java solution against the tests in the body. C++, Java and Go need `signature`: their harnesses are generated from typed literals. The function is a static method of `class Solution`.
Judge a Go solution against the tests in the body. C++, Java and Go need `signature`: their harnesses are generated from typed literals.

request.description: A clean run whose answers are wrong is WA; each test carries the actual value.

exec: pm.test("No tests ran; the error names solution.py", function () {

request.description: A syntax error is a CE verdict (not an HTTP error). No test runs; `error` points at the learner's own file and line.

exec: pm.test("The compiler error names solution.cpp", function () {

request.description: Compiler output comes back in `error`, with paths mapped to solution.cpp.

exec: pm.test("Every test is reported, none passed", function () {

request.description: The process dying (a crash or a non-zero exit) is RE. (An exception raised inside one call is only that test failing: WA.)

exec: pm.test("The first test passed, the second hit the limit", function () {

request.description: `limits` caps the whole run (timeMs 100-10000, memoryMb 32-512). Tests that finished before the limit keep their results; the one running carries the reason; later ones are "not run".
`prelude` sources (same language; not Java) are placed before `code`, e.g. the components a build step depends on.
Caller mistakes are a 400 `{error, details}` before anything runs.

item.name: 03 - Run stream (POST /v1/run/stream)
item.description: The same run as Server-Sent Events: `queued` (only when waiting for a sandbox box), `compiling` (TypeScript, and compiled languages on a compile-cache miss), `running`, one `test` per test in order, then `verdict` (the JSON result without `tests`). An `error` event appears only if the run itself failed. Heartbeat comments (`: keep-alive`) every 15 s.

exec: pm.test("running, three test events in order, then an OK verdict", function () {

request.description: Postman shows the events as they arrive; the tests below run once the stream ends.

item.name: 04 - IDE (POST /v1/ide/execute)
item.description: Whole programs reading stdin and writing stdout, 1-10 test cases, compared on stdout (trailing whitespace ignored). `?wait=true` always answers inline. Without it, a service with REDIS_URL set queues the run and answers 202 `{token, status: "PND"}`; poll GET /v1/ide/execute/:token. Without Redis every request answers inline.

request.description: Each case gets its own process; `testResults[i].status` is OK, WA, TLE, MLE, RE, CE or XX.
Java runs the `public class` it finds (here Main); the class is compiled once for all cases.
Go programs are complete `package main` files.

exec: pm.test("The case is WA with the program's output", function () {

request.description: A clean exit with different stdout is a WA case; `actualOutput` shows what the program printed.

item.name: Submit without wait (202 token when queued)

exec: pm.test("202 with a token (queue on) or 200 with the result (queue off)", function () {

request.description: With REDIS_URL set on the service: 202 `{token, status: "PND"}`, and the token is saved for the next request. Without Redis: 200 with the result, like `?wait=true`.

exec: pm.test("Pending, done, or 404 when nothing was queued", function () {

request.description: Poll with the token from the previous request: `{status: "PND"}` while queued or running, then the full result (kept for QUEUE_RESULT_TTL_SEC). An unknown or expired token, or a service without Redis, answers 404.
At most 10 test cases per request.
